summary: Canada Lookouts logs a Parrott Mountain lookout near Burns Lake: 1939 papers describe trail work and a planned build, and a lookoutman is named in 1944.

events.note: Trail cutting toward the proposed lookout reported in May 1939. A June 1939 item says twelve men would build a lookout. Both describe the work as planned.
Lookoutman F.W. Lindsay named in a Forest Branch News Letter item dated October 20, 1944.

evidence.supports: Parrott Mountain coordinates and elevation on the record

May 24, 1939 (The Interior News): two men cutting trail to the proposed lookout on Parrott Mountain
evidence.quote: May 24, 1939: A.A. Antilla and Wm. Gilgan are busy cutting trail to the proposed look-out on Parrott mountain. (The Interior News)

evidence.supports: June 20, 1939 (The Province): twelve men to build a lookout on Parrott Mountain under the government summer forest programme
evidence.quote: June 20, 1939: Details of projects in the government summer forest programme, which will engage 2295 men, were announced today. In the Prince Rupert district, twelve men will work on protection trails and build a lookout on Parrott Mountain. (The Province)

notes_for_editor: Everything rests on one page, the Canada Lookouts Parrott Mountain entry, which prints a May 1939 Interior News item, a June 1939 Province item and an October 1944 Forest Branch News Letter item. The newspapers themselves were not checked. Several searches found no other page about this lookout. A 2023 Parrot Lookout wildfire result near Francois Lake was not used because it does not concern the site. The entry gives an elevation without a unit, so it is left out of facts. Brief status, access and design were unknown and are left out. The story is short because the evidence is that thin.
